summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and a history of atrial flutter was admitted after experiencing chest pressure following hemodialysis. Initial evaluation revealed elevated troponin levels consistent with a Type II myocardial infarction, likely due to cardiac stress from fluid shifts during dialysis. Her EKG showed multifocal atrial tachycardia, and a chest X-ray was unremarkable. Medication adjustments were made, including holding the morning dose of metoprolol on dialysis days and switching diltiazem to evening dosing only. She tolerated subsequent dialysis sessions without recurrence of symptoms or arrhythmias. She remained stable, was discharged home with updated medication instructions, and advised to follow up for ongoing management.
